paper text.text:
Suppose every bridge with at least two interior vertices has
three attachments and a planar relevant completion. By
Lemma~\ref{dis:relevant}, these bridges have the forms in
Proposition~\ref{prop:three-root-disjoint}. We combine them with
bridges with one interior vertex and the permitted edges, keeping
the interiors disjoint and using the attachment restrictions and
Lemma~\ref{dis:counts}. Four bridges with the same four attachments
would give a $K_{4,4}$ and hence a $K_5$ minor, so we allow at most
three. We use~\supp{E3} when all three paths are edges
and~\supp{E4} when some path has an internal vertex.

These choices include $G$ without having to specify the paths inside
each candidate. By the coverage check in~\supp{E4}, each graph in
this family is a subgraph of a recorded toroidal graph or contains
a recorded nontoroidal graph. Since $G$ is nontoroidal, minimality
gives equality with one of the latter. With at least
one $s_mt_m$ absent, the checks leave $\mathfrak T_{32},\mathfrak
T_{43},\mathfrak T_{61}$ when every bridge has at most one interior
vertex, and $\mathfrak T_{38},\mathfrak T_{45},\mathfrak T_{48},
\mathfrak T_{66},\mathfrak T_{67}$ when some bridge has form $T,S$
or $Q$. No graph with a four-cycle form remains.

the formula.variables: Variable vj of atom A<i> (its list [v1, ..., vm]) means "at least j copies of A<i>". Variables after 456 are auxiliary (cardinality counters).
the formula.base clauses: 6483 clauses: v(j+1) implies vj for each atom, then the constraints of the case listed below.
the formula.one clause per recorded graph: For a toroidal graph with n_i copies of A<i>: the clause that some atom has more copies than in it. For a nontoroidal graph: the clause that some atom in it has fewer copies.
the formula.DRAT check: drat-trim verifies that cover.cnf is unsatisfiable, with the proof cover.drat; the checker of this repository runs it

what this shows: Each allowed assembly is a subgraph of a recorded toroidal graph or contains a recorded nontoroidal graph. By minor minimality, each obstruction in the case is one of the recorded nontoroidal graphs.
not in this item: The genus computations in genus/ certify the recorded nontoroidal graphs (Appendix A).
vertex names: Psi_1 with twins p, q on {s1, s2, s3} and r, z on {t1, t2, t3}. Interior vertices of copy k of atom A<i> are named A<i>#k@<role>. In the forms on {c1, c2, h}, the roles x, y, z are c1, c2, h; for a support containing s_m, t_m they are g, e, h as in Lemma 4.15.
constraints of the case (the base clause: Lemma 3.4(a): an atom whose degree-three interior vertex sees both ends of an edge s_i t_j excludes that edge.
Lemma 4.7: not both s_i t_j and s_j t_i.
At most three bridges on one attachment triple, or four when it contains s_m, t_m and s_m t_m is absent (Lemma 4.16); at most three single vertices on one set {s_i, t_i, s_j, t_j} (most copies 3).
The Q, four-cycle and type (c) forms occur only as the bridge containing P_m: at most one of them for each m, and only when s_m t_m is absent.
For each m, s_m t_m is present or some bridge attaches to both s_m and t_m.

parts.(a): every bridge has at most one interior vertex
